source.title: SOME OPEN QUESTIONS ON ARITHMETIC ZARISKI PAIRS

accepted.question_text: Do the two projective Eyral–Oka curves C+ and C−—a Galois-conjugate pair of irreducible plane sextics of torus type with singularities 2E6 + A5 + A2—form an arithmetic Zariski pair; that is, are the pairs (P², C+) and (P², C−) not homeomorphic even though the curves are Galois conjugate and this paper shows that their projective complement fundamental groups are isomorphic?
accepted.context_brief: Arithmetic Zariski pair status of the original Eyral–Oka sextics

evidence.quote: The question about them being an arithmetic Zariski pair remains open but, using the techniques in [7], several arithmetic Zariski pairs can be exhibited by adding lines to the original curves. It is right hence to conjecture that they form an arithmetic Zariski pair themselves.

In Corollary 2.10, we have proved that the fundamental groups of the Eyral-Oka curves are isomorphic, and hence this invariant cannot be used to decide if these two curves, which are not rigidly equivalent, form an arithmetic Zariski pair.

accepted.question_text: Do the augmented pairs (P², C+ ∪ L+) and (P², C− ∪ L−) form a complement-equivalent Zariski pair; in other words, although the complements of C+ ∪ L+ and C− ∪ L− are homeomorphic (indeed analytically isomorphic), is there nevertheless no homeomorphism of pairs carrying C+ ∪ L+ to C− ∪ L−?
accepted.context_brief: Complement-equivalent Zariski pair question for the curves with distinguished lines

evidence.quote: As we showed in §1, the curves C± ∪L± have homeomorphic complements (even more, analytically isomorphic) via the birational morphism shown in Figure 2. The Cremona transformation that connects both complements is not a homeomorphism of the pairs (P2, C± ∪ L±), so these curves are candidates to be complement equivalent Zariski pairs. We are not able to decide on that problem, but we are apparently more succesful when adding more lines to the original curves C± ∪ L±.

accepted.question_text: For the additional candidate arithmetic Zariski pairs obtained from the Eyral–Oka curves by projecting from the singular points of type E6 or A2, can one prove that the resulting braid monodromy factorizations are not equivalent, thereby distinguishing those pairs topologically?
accepted.context_brief: Non-equivalence of braid monodromies for other projected Eyral–Oka pairs

evidence.quote: Eyral-Oka curves give rise to other arithmetic Zariski pairs, namely using the projections from the singular points of type E6 and A2. When projecting from a point of type E6 it does not matter which one because of the symmetry of the curves which exchanges both points. One can compute the braid monodromy factorizations using again the fact that they are strongly real curves. In these cases, it is more involved to prove that the braid monodromy factorizations are not equivalent. In a future work we will use the computed representations to distinguish the braid monodromies using diagonal representations.
